newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian leaders to tour Europe, warn Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Syrian leaders to tour Europe, warn Netanyahu.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara will tour European countries soon to explain Syria's position on its stalled peace talks with Israel, a senior official said on Monday.

The official, who did not want his name used, renewed Damascus' harsh criticism of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for his refusal to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

In an interview with Reuters the official warned the Israeli premier that Arabs might impose sanctions on Israel if Netanyahu maintains his refusal to withdraw from occupied Arab lands in return for peace.

In the Cairo summit last June shortly after Netanyahu was elected, Arab countries warned Israel not to deviate from the concept of trading land for peace and said they would reconsider the ties made since peace talks started in 1991 if this happened.
The Syrian official blasted the Israeli premier's pledge to build 6,500 Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 war, was "an example of Netanyahu's hostility to peace."

"While Syria expresses readiness to resume peace talks with Israel, Netanyahu insists on ignoring the outcome of talks which were conducted with his predecessors.. he also comes up with new plans to build more Jewish homes in the occupied Arab lands," the official said.
Netanyahu, who took office in June, says he would take note of talks held with the previous Israeli Labour-led government but would not commit himself to any agreements made by that government.
Syria says the Labour government agreed during the talks, which were suspended last March after a spate of suicide bombings in Israel, to withdraw from the Golan Heights.
"If we use Netanyahu's logic and cancel the outcome of talks or agreements with governments when a new cabinet is formed this means that negotiations might go on forever," the official said.
The Syrian official said exact dates for the Syrian leaders' tour, which would include stops in the major European capitals, were being finalised.
